name: Andromeda
alt: A long Hubble mosaic of Andromeda, with a glowing yellow center, dark dust lanes, blue outer stars, and jagged mosaic edges.
credit: NASA, ESA, B. Williams (University of Washington)
imageNote: NASA/ESA Hubble photomosaic released in January 2025.

facts.label: Distinctive feature
facts.value: The 2025 Hubble mosaic resolves the light of about 200 million stars, giving astronomers a detailed record of Andromeda’s history of mergers.

description: The 2025 Hubble mosaic resolves the light of about 200 million stars, giving astronomers a detailed record of Andromeda’s history of mergers.

name: Triangulum
alt: Triangulum’s inner spiral arms, filled with countless stars, dark dust clouds, and bright blue nebulae.
credit: NASA, ESA, and M. Durbin, J. Dalcanton, and B. F. Williams (University of Washington)
imageNote: Hubble mosaic of the central region and inner spiral arms.

facts.label: Type
facts.value: Spiral galaxy without a central bar

facts.label: Distinctive feature
facts.value: The Local Group’s third-largest galaxy has no bright central bulge; its abundant gas and dust sustain active star formation.

description: The Local Group’s third-largest galaxy has no bright central bulge; its abundant gas and dust sustain active star formation.

name: Whirlpool
alt: The Whirlpool Galaxy’s two blue spiral arms and pink star-forming regions, beside its smaller golden companion NGC 5195.
credit: NASA, ESA, S. Beckwith (STScI), and The Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)
imageNote: Hubble image of M51 and its companion NGC 5195.

facts.label: Distinctive feature
facts.value: Its two sweeping spiral arms compress hydrogen gas, creating bright star-forming regions and young blue star clusters.

facts.label: Companion
facts.value: The smaller yellow galaxy NGC 5195 passes behind M51; their interaction may help make the spiral pattern prominent.

description: Its two sweeping spiral arms compress hydrogen gas, creating bright star-forming regions and young blue star clusters. The smaller yellow galaxy NGC 5195 passes behind M51; their interaction may help make the spiral pattern prominent.

name: Sombrero
alt: The nearly edge-on Sombrero Galaxy, with a bright white central bulge wrapped by a sharply defined dark dust ring.
imageNote: Hubble mosaic with updated processing, released in April 2025.

facts.label: Type
facts.value: Galaxy with both spiral and elliptical features

facts.label: Distinctive feature
facts.value: Viewed only about six degrees above its equatorial plane, its dust-rich disk cuts a dark band across a brilliant central bulge.

description: Viewed only about six degrees above its equatorial plane, its dust-rich disk cuts a dark band across a brilliant central bulge.

name: Milky Way
alt: Artist’s concept of the Milky Way viewed from above, with a bright elongated central bar and blue spiral arms on black space.
credit: NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center/Conceptual Image Lab
imageNote: Artist’s concept of the Milky Way

facts.label: Our location
facts.value: Inside the galaxy, about 26,000 light-years from its center

facts.label: Distinctive feature
facts.value: The Sun lies in the Orion Arm. Because we observe the galaxy from within, external views of the Milky Way are scientific illustrations.

description: The Sun lies in the Orion Arm. Because we observe the galaxy from within, external views of the Milky Way are scientific illustrations.
